ConnectionStrings.//Default: The local development database, in the Postgres container the README starts. A deployment overrides this with ConnectionStrings__Default, which may hold either this keyword form or the postgresql:// URL a managed host publishes — both are understood.

Jwt.//SigningKey: Deliberately absent. Startup fails with a clear message until one is supplied out of source control — appsettings.Development.json locally (it is gitignored), the environment or a vault in deployment.

EmailSettings.//: SMTP, over MailKit. The password is deliberately absent, like the signing key — supply it out of source control: appsettings.Development.json locally (gitignored), the environment or a vault in deployment. Empty is allowed in Development only, where reset codes go to the console instead of an inbox; outside Development startup fails without it, because a server that cannot send mail cannot reset a password.
EmailSettings.//Password: On Gmail this must be an app password from a 2FA-enabled account. The account's own password does not authenticate against SMTP at all.

RateLimit.//: Auth requests allowed per address per window. Raise it for a deployment behind a NAT that many readers share.

Google.//ClientId: The **Web** OAuth client ID, which is the audience a device asks Google to mint its ID token for. Not a secret — the same value ships inside the APK. There is deliberately no client secret: this app verifies ID tokens rather than trading authorization codes, so a secret would be a credential we store and never use. Leave empty to turn Google sign-in off.
